text:
Jules (AM): Quick sync — Acme POC readout tomorrow at 11. Need final agreement on success metrics + outstanding blockers.
Priya (SE): Thanks — I’ll bring the demo results. TL;DR: latency & cost look good, but we saw a 6% drop on the entity-extraction eval after quantizing to int8.
Samir (PM): Can you share the exact eval prompt set and pass threshold you used? we should align on acceptance criteria beforehand.
Priya (SE): Prompt set: 120 prompts saved in /evals/acme_entity_v2.csv (I’ll paste sample below). Acceptance idea: F1 >= 0.88 and no regression > 5% vs baseline.
Priya (SE): Sample prompts:
```
1. "Extract company names from: 'Redwood Inference helps teams...'"
2. "List product features from: 'Our product has X, Y, Z'"
```
Jules (AM): Customer expects p99 latency < 250ms for single-turn inference and cost per 1k tokens under our committed price tier. Is that realistic?
Marta (SRE): On dedicated pool yes. Our current stress run (50 rps sustained) gave p99=210ms with batching=auto. We need to keep batch size cap to preserve latency.
Ben (Security): Quick sec checklist for readout — they still want: SOC2 report, KMS integration details, and confirmation of data residency (EU). We have SOC2 link in confluence but need to confirm KMS design for private deployment.
Samir (PM): Action: Priya to attach eval csv + result summary by EOD. Ben to paste KMS design snippet and EU-region availability. Marta to confirm p99 numbers and the exact config used. Jules to own commercial ask (final price band).
Priya (SE): Uploaded eval summary: overall F1=0.892 on fp16 baseline, int8=0.835. Breakdown attached. Notable: short prompts with many rare tokens caused the biggest drop.
Jules (AM): Customer will push back on int8 quality. Two asks: 1) is there a middle ground (mixed precision / per-layer quant) 2) if they accept int8, can we offer a temporary price concession for first 3 months?
Priya (SE): We can try mixed-precision (quantize attention only) — prototype config reduced quality drop to 2.3% loss (F1=0.872). More infra testing required.
Ben (Security): For KMS: we can do customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge in private deploys. For hosted, we support envelope encryption and BYOK for enterprise plans — I’ll paste the snippet: "KMS flow: CMK -> envelope key -> per-token keys stored ephemeral".
Samir (PM): Good. Also we need to call out SSO and SCIM — customer asked for SCIM provisioning and groups mapping to roles. Is that done?
Marta (SRE): SCIM is available on Dedicated and Private, not for self-serve hosted yet. We can enable for their org on dedicated. Need their IdP metadata.
Jules (AM): I'll ask for IdP metadata today. Also pricing: propose provisional pricing bands: committed 2x reserved GPUs -> $X/month, overage at $Y/token. If they push back, we can offer a 12-week ramp credit. Thoughts?
Samir (PM): Offer structure sounds fine. Make the ramp credit contingent on completing the quality gate (F1 >= 0.88 on accepted prompt set) and security checklist (SOC2 + KMS confirmation).
Priya (SE): Potential blocker: firewall rules — private deploy requires outbound to our telemetry endpoints; customer legal may block that. If they want fully air-gapped, timeline jumps.
Ben (Security): We can provide an air-gapped package but requires extra controls and a 6–8 week delivery lead time. Note for readout: flag this as an escalation path, not the default.
Jules (AM): For readout agenda: 1) Executive summary (Samir) 2) Demo (Priya) 3) Metrics + evals (Priya/Marta) 4) Security (Ben) 5) Commercial (Jules) 6) Next steps & timeline (all).
Samir (PM): Also prepare a one-pager with final pass/fail table: latency, throughput, F1, cost delta, SSO, KMS — we’ll use that to decide expansion. I can draft.
Priya (SE): One more note: the model variant used in production vs our test set differed (we tested a trimmed tokenizer). Need to standardize the model artifact id for apples-to-apples. I’ll include exact model sha in the readout.
ops-bot: deployment-check: dedicated-pool-acme: replicas=4, gpu_type=A10G, autoscale=on
Marta (SRE): Ops-bot output matches my runs. For the readout I’ll include the JMeter run command and the config:
```
jmeter -n -t acme_poc.jmx -Jthreads=50 -Jduration=1800
```
Jules (AM): Good. Final asks before readout: Priya attach csv + diff report, Ben attach KMS snippet + SOC2 link, Marta attach raw latency logs, Samir finalize one-pager. I’ll send calendar invite and include stakeholders.
Samir (PM): Timeline: readout tomorrow 11; by EOD today we need all artifacts in the folder /sales/acme/poc-readout. If anything slips, flag it here.
Priya (SE): On it — uploading now.
Ben (Security): Uploaded SOC2 redacted, KMS summary doc.
Marta (SRE): Uploaded latency logs and jmeter report.
Jules (AM): Thanks everyone — see you tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Priya (SE): Quick note for meeting: if customer declines mixed precision, fallback plan is to run fp16 on dedicated but with increased cost. I’ll have exact delta numbers in the one-pager.
Samir (PM): Perfect. Closing thread for prep. If new blocker appears post-EOD, create a follow-up thread.
